newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish steel maker reduces public share issue.
newsitem.headline: Polish steel maker reduces public share issue.

text.p: Polish steel maker Stalprodukt SA has decided to cut its planned initial public offering by more than half to avoid unfavourable pricing or high costs of underwriting, its president said on Wednesday.
The company, which earlier planned to sell between 2.3 and three million shares, will now offer between 800,000 and 1.2 million shares, Piotr Janeczek told a news conference.
He said the size of the issue was cut because too many other public offerings were planned for this year.

"Because of the situation on the stock market it was very probable that our issue would not take place or, if it did, the share price would be low and costs of underwriting would be too high," he said.

He said Stalprodukt planned to offer up to 800,000 shares in a large-investors tranche in a subscription between April 14 and 19. Small investors will be offered up to 400,000 shares between April 14 and 16.
The earning from the issue, forecast at between 24 and 30 million zlotys, will be invested in boosting the production of electrotechnical steel, he said.
Stalprodukt is 40-percent owned by the Krakow-based Huta Sendzimira steel mill, with the remaining shares held by an employee-controlled company.

The company estimates that its net profit reached 21 million zlotys last year, compared with 19 million zlotys in 1995, on sales of an estimated 315-318 million zlotys and 297 million zlotys respectively.
